project_transform.conversion: x = e - origin_e; z = origin_n - n

authoritative_target.selection_reason: The live OSM stadium semantic envelope intersects exactly these two versioned UrbIS construction features by more than 1 m2. Both are almost entirely inside that semantic envelope and share the same official UrbIS block. OSM is used only to identify the semantic stadium envelope; the selected geometry and target centroid remain UrbIS-derived.

full_urbis_union_game_xz.conversion: x = e - origin_e; z = origin_n - n

terrain_elevation.method: Bilinear interpolation of four valid committed 5 m UrbIS DTM runtime samples; no extrapolation or NoData substitution.

semantic_cross_check.role: semantic envelope complement only; never final game geometry

official_dimension_cross_check.source: King Baudouin Stadium official website — The Stadium in figures
official_dimension_cross_check.role: validation only; dimensions do not replace UrbIS geometry
official_dimension_cross_check.uncertainty: The selected UrbIS construction union has a larger oriented rectangle than the official stadium dimensions. This is retained as an explicit semantic/footprint mismatch rather than manually shrinking or reshaping authoritative geometry.

orthophoto_cross_check.source: Paradigm / Brussels-Capital Region official raster WMS

camera_policy.rule: Render both official Atomium observation-level candidates toward this UrbIS-derived stadium target without claiming either candidate as the 2007 photographer position. Preserve provisional FOV/crop status until visual comparison is complete.

provenance_notes: UrbIS remains the authoritative geometry source.
OSM is used only as a semantic selector/cross-check and is separately attributed under ODbL 1.0.
Official stadium dimensions are used only to detect gross semantic mismatches.
The frozen 2024 official orthophoto covers the target and is used for visual cross-checking.
The target ground elevation is derived only from the committed UrbIS DTM runtime and its pinned bilinear sample evidence.
Game X/Z is derived from the canonical Laeken/Jette project transform used by anchors.json; Z increases southward.
No manual geometry or elevation was introduced to force agreement between sources.
